records.name: 1a. Feed system and cycle (Axis C)
records.detail: The repository models exactly one architecture: electric-pump-fed. Adding any turbine-driven cycle needs a turbine model and a gas-generator model, neither of which exists in any form. Adding a pressure-fed upper stage needs a non-regen chamber model. | # | Document | ID | Supplies | Blocks | |---|---|---|---|---| | G1 | **NASA SP-8110**, *Liquid Rocket Engine Turbines* (Jan 1974, 158 pp) | ✅ NTRS [19740026132](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19740026132) | Turbine type selection, admission, velocity-ratio efficiency, blade stress, temperature limits, installation | **Every pump-fed cycle except electric.** There is no turbine model in the repository, so gas-generator and staged-combustion cycles cannot close their power balance at all |

records.quote: ### 1b. Thermochemistry (Axis B) — the largest single hole found
records.detail: The entire property-surface layer depends on CEA. **No CEA primary reference is in the corpus** — only papers that cite it. R5b (held-out property validation) is on the critical path in `ROADMAP_REQUIREMENTS_TO_PARTS.md`, and a validation report cannot be written against a code with no specification on hand. | # | Document | ID | Supplies | Blocks | |---|---|---|---|---| | G4 | Gordon & McBride, **NASA RP-1311 Part I**, *Computer Program for Calculation of Complex Chemical Equilibrium Compositions and Applications: I. Analysis* (1994) | ✅ NTRS [19950013764](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19950013764) | The assumptions, governing equations and solution method behind every `c*`, γ and `T_c` the tool reports; rocket-performance, shock and detonation applications | R5b held-out validation; any defensible statement about what the property surfaces are approximating |

records.name: 1c. Real-fluid coolant and propellant properties (Axis B)
records.quote: ### 1c. Real-fluid coolant and propellant properties (Axis B)
records.detail: `MissionSpec` carries `rho_cool`, `cp_cool`, `k_cool`, `mu_cool` as four scalars. For "any fuel" that has to become a fluid model, and the two fuels the repository most needs are exactly the two CoolProp does not have. | # | Document | ID | Supplies | Blocks | |---|---|---|---|---| | G7 | Huber, Lemmon, Ott & Bruno, *Preliminary Surrogate Mixture Models for the Thermophysical Properties of Rocket Propellants RP-1 and RP-2*, **Energy & Fuels** 23(6), 2009 | ✅ DOI [10.1021/ef900216z](https://doi.org/10.1021/ef900216z) | Four-component RP-1 surrogate (α-methyldecalin, n-dodecane, 5-methylnonane, heptylcyclohexane) fitted to density, sound speed, viscosity, thermal conductivity and advanced distillation curves. Quoted 95 %-confidence accuracy: density 0.4 %, sound speed 2 %, viscosity 2 %, thermal conductivity 4 %, distillation 0.5 % | **CoolProp has no RP-1.** This is the only route from four constants to a validated fluid, and it comes with its own error bars — which is what R5b needs |

records.name: 1d. The cooling failure mode not currently screened (Axis B)
records.quote: ### 1d. The cooling failure mode not currently screened (Axis B)
records.detail: The coking constraint (SP-8087, 728 K for RP-1) is a **hydrocarbon** mechanism. `mdo/propellants.py` correctly sets it to `None` for hydrogen. But nothing replaces it — and for methane and hydrogen the governing coolant-side failure is heat-transfer deterioration, which the repository does not screen at all. | # | Document | ID | Supplies | Blocks | |---|---|---|---|---| | G10 | Nasuti & Pizzarelli, *Pseudo-boiling and heat transfer deterioration while heating supercritical liquid rocket engine propellants*, **J. Supercritical Fluids** 168:105066, 2021 | ✅ DOI [10.1016/j.supflu.2020.105066](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.supflu.2020.105066) | HTD onset conditions, the pseudo-boiling mechanism, and the role of exit-to-critical pressure ratio and surface roughness in avoiding it | A **methane or hydrogen** cooling constraint. Without it, LOX/LCH4 and LOX/LH2 designs are unconstrained on the coolant side, which will read as "feasible" when it is really "unmodelled". The corpus already has Pizzarelli 2015 (supercritical methane *modelling*, PAPER-0207/0208) but not the deterioration review |

records.name: 6. Suggested acquisition order
records.detail: Resolving SP-8109's reference list changed this order substantially: several items that looked like open-ended searches turned out to be named NACA/NASA reports that are probably free. **Batch 1 — free or near-free, and each unblocks a track.** One session of downloading. | Get | What it unblocks | |---|---| | **NACA Report 936** (Brown & Bradshaw 1949) — H2 | the friction-corrected volute law → Track H5 → the radial load Track J needs | | **NASA CR-72965 / CR-72966** — H2b, low-thrust pumps | Track L's envelope question, at the exact thrust class where the stack currently crashes | | **NASA CR-72630** (Watters & Luehr 1970) — H1b | balance pistons and hydrostatic bearings, i.e. the branch an electric pump at 30–60 krpm actually needs |

records.name: H10 — Rotordynamics of high-speed pumps
records.detail: **Candidate:** a rotordynamics text covering critical-speed calculation (transfer-matrix or finite-element), bearing and seal stiffness and damping coefficients, and subsynchronous whirl stability. **Why:** SP-8101 (item 14) may supply the turbopump-specific method, but the Lomakin effect — the rotordynamic stiffness of an annular seal or wear ring, which is a *design variable the toolkit controls* through clearance — needs a general treatment. SP-8109 §2.2.1.1 warns about subsynchronous whirl instability above the first critical without giving a stability criterion.

records.name: H11 — Cryogenic and propellant-lubricated bearing practice
records.quote: ### H11 — Cryogenic and propellant-lubricated bearing practice
records.detail: **Why:** SP-8048 (item 13) is from 1971. If the toolkit is to serve LOX and methane electric-pump designs at modern speeds, a current source on propellant-lubricated and hybrid-ceramic bearings would materially change the design space. Lower priority than item 13 itself — get the monograph first, then judge whether this is needed. ---

records.name: H12 — SP-8109 figures 3, 5, 13, 16 and 21, digitized
records.detail: **Not an acquisition — a task.** The PDF is held. These figures carry numbers the OCR cannot recover and that the tree either needs or would materially benefit from: | Figure | Contents | Use | |---|---|---| | **5** | efficiency vs specific speed, with δ = D_t1/D_t2 as a second parameter, plus cavitation bands | **The natural upgrade to `pump_efficiency`** (`mdo/pump.py:50`), whose docstring already concedes it is a screening surrogate, not a fit — and which currently has no δ dependence at all | | **13** | pump performance vs geometry for NERVA, X-8 LH2, J-2 LOX, F-1 LOX, H-1 RP-1, H-1 LOX, 350K LH2, with φ₂, ψ, Z₂, β₂, D_t1/D_t2 | **Seven flight-hardware benchmark points.** The OCR interleaves the columns and cannot be trusted; rendered, this is an immediate validation set |

records.name: H13 — SP-8109 equations (20) and (21), rendered
records.detail: The diffuser-vane / impeller-blade **wave reinforcement** criterion. The prose is clear — reinforcement occurs when the index m is an integer, over Z₂, Z_d, πD_v, the speed of sound a, and the mean relative velocity W — but both equations are OCR-scrambled. Track H5 needs them before coding the vane-count gate. Same for **equation (22)**, the preliminary blade thickness `t ≈ 0.087 b_t2 U_t2 / (sin β_t2 σ_allow)`: the constant and the form should be seen before being implemented, since it would replace a geometric ratio with a structural one.

Perakis 2021 (`perakis2021.pdf`, already held) does the last of these as an inverse problem and may be sufficient on its own; read it before requesting more. --- - **A GD&T standard.** ASME Y14.5-2018, Y14.24-2012 and Y14.41-2003 are all in the

records.name: H3 — Pump performance test standard
records.detail: **Blocks:** Track K1's acceptance conventions and K2's adjudication. **Nothing in `propulsion_texts/` defines a test *procedure*.** SP-8109 gives *conventions* — its fig. 4 data are at **2 % head loss for pumps and 10 % for inducers**, notably *not* the commercial 3 % — but not how to run the test, how many points, at what stabilisation criteria, or how to reduce the data. **Candidates:** **ISO 9906** *Rotodynamic pumps — Hydraulic performance acceptance tests*, or **ANSI/HI 14.6**, or **ASME PTC 8.2** *Centrifugal Pumps*. **Must contain:** the H–Q–η–NPSH test procedure, required instrumentation and its

records.name: H4 — Measurement uncertainty framework
records.detail: **Blocks:** the `uncertainty` field of the measurement record meaning anything, and therefore K2's ability to say whether a residual is significant. **Candidates:** **ISO/IEC Guide 98-3 (GUM)**, *Guide to the Expression of Uncertainty in Measurement*; or **ASME PTC 19.1** *Test Uncertainty*. **Must contain:** Type A vs Type B evaluation, combined standard uncertainty, coverage factors and expanded uncertainty, propagation through a data-reduction equation, and correlated-input treatment. The last is not optional here: c\* is computed from P_c, A_t and ṁ, whose errors are not independent. **Note:** Reis 2019 — the most complete pump test in the corpus — quotes **no

records.name: H5 — Flow measurement standard
records.detail: **Blocks:** the largest single uncertainty term in any pump or injector test. **Candidate:** **ISO 5167** (parts 1–4), *Measurement of fluid flow by means of pressure differential devices inserted in circular cross-section conduits*. **Must contain:** orifice, nozzle and venturi discharge coefficients with their uncertainty, installation and straight-length requirements, expansibility, and the Reynolds-number range of validity. Reis 2019 uses "flowmeters" and a "calibrated orifice" with neither coefficient nor uncertainty stated. ---

records.name: H6 — Achievable tolerance and fits by process
records.quote: ### H6 — Achievable tolerance and fits by process
records.detail: **Candidates:** **ISO 2768** (general tolerances), **ISO 286** (ISO system of limits and fits). Optionally a machining-practice handbook for achievable-tolerance-by- process tables. **Why:** ASME Y14.5-2018 is already in the corpus and defines the *language* of tolerance — datums, feature control frames, material conditions. It does not say what a process can *achieve*. Track I1's `achievable_tolerance` field and Track J5's cold-vs-operating fit statements both need the values, and `COMPLETION_PLAN.md` G5 is currently blocked partly on this.

records.name: H7 — Bolted joint preload and a selected fastener family
records.quote: ### H7 — Bolted joint preload and a selected fastener family
records.detail: **Candidate:** **VDI 2230** *Systematic calculation of highly stressed bolted joints*, plus a selected NAS/MS/ISO fastener standard. **Why:** already flagged in `COMPLETION_PLAN.md` §10 as "partial — request fastener selection/standards". SP-8109 §2.4.3.2 covers fasteners and attachments at the practice level; the preload calculation and the fastener catalogue are elsewhere. Track J6 and the split-casing work both need it.

records.name: H8 — Turbomachinery blade geometry and flank milling
records.quote: ### H8 — Turbomachinery blade geometry and flank milling
records.detail: **Candidate:** a turbomachinery blade-design reference covering ruled-surface blade definition and 5-axis flank milling geometry — for example a text on the geometric definition of ruled blade surfaces and cutter-path generation, or a CAM-side treatment of flank-milling error for ruled and near-ruled surfaces. **Why:** Track H3 must decide whether a generated blade is flank-millable or must be point-milled, and Track I2 must check tool reachability against the answer. SP-8109 constrains this from the outside (`Z₂ ≤ 28 sin β₂`, cutter L/D ≤ 10 / 8) but never defines the surface geometry. `propulsion_texts/L-05_BSplines_NURBS.pdf` and

records.name: H9 — Inverse / prescribed-loading blade design
records.detail: **Candidate:** a treatment of centrifugal impeller blade design by prescribed blade loading or prescribed velocity distribution. **Why:** Track H1 must choose a β(u) distribution. SP-8109 says only that the distribution "and the blade number are adjusted until desired design limits are achieved", with velocity gradients checked for eddies and separation. That is a criterion without a method. The default (linear in r, as now) is defensible as a starting point; anything better needs a source.
